correctness.rationale: For N=3^n+1, n>=1, reconstruct digit-complement definition and ternary carry count: antipalindrome length equals digit sum; two-summand digits force lengths n and n-2 and a single carry transition. Length gaps >=4 and same-length pair except n=2 are impossible. Complement symmetry forces unique alternating middle digits for even n>=6 and excludes odd n. Verify explicit B_n=3^(n-3)+1+2 sum_(j=1)^(n/2-2)3^(2j), A_n=3^n+1-B_n, and 3-summand 1+U_n+V_n, with n=1,2,4 boundaries. Independently generated all admissible ternary antipalindromes up to N=3^16+1 and exhaustively counted unordered two-sums for n=1..16: exactly claimed H values and unique pair whenever two summands possible. Only the symbolic carry argument proves all n.
